title: StableGrasp: single-image hand grasp reconstruction using differentiable physics simulation
summary: StableGrasp separates visual hand pose estimation from grasping control targets, minimizing grasp kinetic energy within a differentiable physics simulation to generate physically stable hand-object interactions from single RGB images while preserving visual and geometric consistency.
research_notes:
Provide a single RGB image capturing a hand-object grasp along with the 3D model of the target object.

Initialize visual hand pose estimates using an upstream image-based 3D hand pose estimator.

Initialize grasp control targets separately from the visual hand pose parameters.

Run differentiable physics simulation minimizing grasp kinetic energy alongside geometric and visual alignment losses.

Extract the optimized physically stable 3D hand mesh and corresponding control forces for robotics simulation or virtual interaction.

Decouple visual pose parameters from physical control targets rather than directly translating visual joint poses into control torques.

Combine grasp kinetic energy minimization in differentiable simulation with geometric regularization against the input image to avoid unnatural hand mesh deformation.

Deploy the framework as a downstream physical refinement step on top of existing vision-based hand pose estimators to eliminate object penetration and drop failures.
